revisionNote: 2026-10-26: two deliberate changes. (1) The particle layer was toned down (fewer visible dust specks, matched to the reference frame), so the canonical-capture baselines for frame, top background, category icon row and item label row were re-measured on the current feature build: frame 18.02/0.8301, top background 20.24/0.9344, category icon row 21.05/0.8950, item label row 11.94/0.3910; clock and info bar are unchanged. (2) The Game column was reshaped: Steam Store, then one All Games folder (detail = distinct Steam titles, 282), then the dev_flash utilities. The inline installed rows and the top-level Not Installed row are gone; Not Installed is now reached through All Games (folder mode library, 275 rows). The named-state recipes and their self-baseline references were refreshed for that shape. The stored-pair baselines above remain the historical RPCS3 comparison numbers and are unchanged. (3) The clock now defaults to the American format the user asked for (MM/DD date, 12-hour time, one space), so the canonical clock text and info bar no longer match the DD/MM 24-hour RPCS3 reference frame by design: their captureBaseline is re-measured at 11.39/0.4105 and 14.78/0.6117. Switching clock/dateFormat and clock/hourFormat back to DD/MM + 24-hour reproduces the reference string and scores 13.61/0.6226 and 17.21/0.7114. (4) 2026-10-27, phase 5.1: eight named states were added for the surfaces that had none - the Triangle options panel on a folder page, a notification, the volume HUD, a subtitle cue, Continue Watching populated and empty, the Jellyfin sign-in page and the Download Management page. Each has a recipe, dump/sidecar/log assertions and its own deliberately saved native reference under out/native-reference/layers/; the four existing Steam references were not regenerated and still score inf/1.0000 on this build. The capture exe now names the integration build the references were saved from, and the named-state runner gained column-aware routes (a recipe may start in another XMB column), rowIndex stages for pages the build writes no dump for, per-state env, pre-grab/post-grab script tokens, sidecar range assertions and log assertions.

baselinePair.note: Stored 1920x1080 native capture of the settled Game root menu, scored against the stored RPCS3 frame. This pair is the historical baseline: whole frame 18.20 dB / 0.8388 SSIM. Offline scoring of this pair is deterministic, so its gate catches tooling (decoder/metric/crop) regressions.

tolerance.rationale: Two canonical capture runs are pixel-identical (PSNR Infinity, SSIM 1.0000), so run-to-run jitter contributes nothing. The budget therefore only absorbs GPU/driver shader noise and small environment drift. 0.5 dB PSNR is a 12% MSE increase, while a visible layer regression (a moved icon, a dropped label row, a shifted gradient) moves a layer score by more than 1 dB; 0.004 SSIM is likewise far above observed noise and far below a visible regression.

capture.note: Canonical capture recipe. All animation clocks are pinned, so two runs are pixel-identical. XMB_STEAM_ROOT points at an empty directory: the stored RPCS3 reference frame's Game column predates this PC's Steam library and shows the dev_flash XMBML entries only. backgroundClock 10:00 is the traced daytime mapping used by the stored baseline; uiClock matches the reference frame's 25/10 12:32. The default exe is the integration build this file's named-state references were last saved from; pass --exe when the integration build moves.

layers.name: frame
layers.description: Whole 1920x1080 frame (aggregate; not a layer by itself)

layers.name: top background
layers.description: Upper-left background gradient and glare, no clock, no category icons

layers.name: category icon row
layers.description: Full-width band across the category icons and their spacing

layers.name: item label row
layers.description: Focused item row: icon plus glowing label. Content still differs from the reference, so this is a regression gate, not a fidelity pass

layers.name: clock text
layers.description: Digits of the top-right date/time only

layers.name: info bar
layers.description: Top-right info bar: translucent band, border and analog clock icon, including its text

stateSelfBaseline.rationale: Named states have no RPCS3 frame: their reference is the deterministic native render itself, so a fresh capture must reproduce that frame (self-baseline regression gate, not firmware fidelity). Two runs of every state are byte-identical on this machine (PSNR Infinity, SSIM 1.0000). 55 dB still catches any deterministic drawing change (one changed 255-level pixel already costs ~68 dB on a 1080p frame) while leaving room for GPU/driver shader noise; 0.9995 SSIM is the same margin. Refresh a reference deliberately after an intended rendering or layout change with --states --save-reference.

states.name: steam-game-root
states.description: Game column root after the reshape: Steam Store, one All Games folder (detail = distinct Steam titles), then the dev_flash utilities. No inline installed rows and no top-level Not Installed row.

states.name: steam-all-games
states.description: All Games page: All Titles, then one folder per non-empty Steam collection (collection-name order), then Not Installed and Family Shared. Only the 14 folder rows are asserted, not the title lists inside them.

states.name: steam-store-sections
states.description: Steam Store page opened from the Game column: Top Sellers / New Releases / Specials. The sections page makes no store request, so it needs no network.

states.name: steam-not-installed
states.description: Not Installed folder opened through All Games: owned-but-not-installed rows plus the seeded family-shared titles. Only the visible first rows are scored; the folder dump bounds the row count.

states.name: xmb-notification
states.description: A notification pop-up over the settled Game root, raised through Shell::notify - the same path a real event uses, not a drawing test. The plaque sits under the information bar; the sidecar reports the queued pop-up and its icon, and the log reports the enqueue.

states.name: xmb-volume-hud
states.description: The transient volume HUD at a pinned 25%, driven through the VOLSET script token (the same apply path the Windows media keys use); VOLRESTORE puts the endpoint back after the grab. The HUD has no sidecar field, so its level is asserted from the app's own read-back line, which records what Windows reported after the write.

states.name: video-options-panel
states.description: The Triangle options panel open on the Video Library folder page: Open / Information / Sort By / Close with the focus glow on Open, over the dimmed page. The panel is a composite, not a page, so its own log line and the page's sidecar rows are the state oracle.

log.pattern: shell: options opened category= video depth= 1 .*rows= 4 Open\|Information\|Sort By\|Close

states.name: continue-watching
states.description: Continue Watching populated from a seeded resume record: the Video column's first row opens the page built from media/resume, one row for the remembered file with its Resume at line.

log.pattern: continue watching: page opened with 1 row\(s\)

states.name: continue-watching-empty
states.description: Continue Watching with no remembered positions: the row reports the firmware's own empty state as a dialog over the Video column instead of opening an empty page.

states.name: subtitle-cue
states.description: A sidecar subtitle cue over local media paused at position 0: the fixture clip plus its own .srt, opened from the Video Library page. Pausing and then seeking left clamps to exactly 0, so the video frame, the 0:00 controls and the first cue are the same on every run. The sidecar reports the cue number, its file and the position; the log reports the sidecar discovery.

states.name: jellyfin-signin
states.description: The in-XMB Jellyfin sign-in page opened from a registered Jellyfin service row in the TV column (the seeded apps.json registration, no server contacted). Five rows, focus on Username, the registration URL shown read-only, and the page, not a modal widget.

log.pattern: jellyfin: sign-in page opened rows= Server URL\|Username\|Password\|Sign In\|Cancel focus= Username

states.name: steam-download-page
states.description: Download Management in the Network column, listing a fixture Steam download queue (four manifests in scanner order: active, paused, queued, pending). The page's own .dl.json dump asserts the rows, their state text and their details; the fixture root comes from the recipe's env, so the machine's real Steam queue cannot change the state.

log.pattern: steam downloads: page opened with 4 row\(s\)
